sonnet.problem: The card says the psalmist is speaking to "God's people." Verse 1 gives no addressee, so the card adds one the text doesn't state.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The question is verse 2 with one word blanked. No earlier card gives any context to reason out "thanksgiving" (card 1 told only verse 1), so the baker can only guess the wording of the line. Offerings and incense are equally plausible.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: Card 12 just told that the fathers tested and tried God there. This True statement repeats that and adds a second claim ("even though they had seen His work"), so it tests two claims and mostly re-asks what the card before it said.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim. ... A True statement never just repeats the card before it.
